subject: Banking
title: The Interchange Fee Machine
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Interchange Fee Machine.

hook.text: Every card swipe costs the merchant 1.5-3.5% in fees. On $5 trillion in US card volume.

buildup.text: Interchange fees flow from the merchant's bank to the cardholder's bank. The card network takes a small cut too.

discovery.text: Your bank uses interchange revenue to fund rewards. Your cashback and airline miles are paid by merchants.

twist.text: Small businesses pay the same rates as large chains but can't negotiate. Interchange hits independent shops hardest.

climax.text: Card rewards are a wealth transfer. Merchants pay fees, card users get perks. Cash users subsidize everyone.

punchline.text: $160 billion in swipe fees. Merchants fund your airline miles.

quiz.question: Who ultimately pays for credit card rewards programs?

details.summary: Interchange fees are charges paid by merchants' banks to cardholders' banks on every card transaction, typically 1.5 to 3 percent, generating over 100 billion dollars annually and funding card rewards programs.
details.whyItMatters: Interchange fees are effectively a hidden tax on all card purchases that merchants pass on to consumers through higher prices. Even cash-paying customers subsidize credit card rewards they never receive.
takeaways: Merchants pay 1.5 to 3 percent per credit card transaction in interchange
These fees fund cash-back rewards, airline miles, and card perks
Cash-paying consumers effectively subsidize card-using consumers

faq.question: Why are interchange fees so high in the United States?
faq.answer: Limited regulation and the dominance of Visa and Mastercard allow high fees. The EU caps interchange by law at 0.3 percent for credit cards. The US has only regulated debit card interchange through the Durbin Amendment.

faq.question: Do interchange fees make prices higher for everyone?
faq.answer: Yes. Merchants generally set the same price regardless of payment method, building the interchange cost into the price. This means cash-paying customers pay the same prices that include a hidden card-fee subsidy for card users.
